cA.text: A · Controls on each panel. Closest to the Companion: every panel carries Tax, Damage, Mana and Counters. Commander damage turns the table around the player taking it. Shared game options sit in the center button.

cB.text: B · Shared spine. Panels hold only name, life and badges for what's in play. A spine down the middle holds everything shared: turn, day/night, monarch, initiative, dice, undo. Combat starts from the attacker, so one swing at several players is one entry.

cC.text: C · One marker, own drawer. Panels stay clean, with one marker each (Hugh's marker rule). It opens that player's own sheet, turned to face them, with Damage, Counters, Tax and Mana tabs. Commander damage is a grid of the opponents' commanders.

rows.text:
Top row: the same moment in all three, mid-game on a phone lying flat. Colin's turn 7, Peter on 3 poison, Max is the monarch, You just took 3.

Bottom row: Colin's Ghalta has hit Peter for 14 commander damage, and the player logs it.

The seats face the phone's long edges. Tablet and 2, 3, 5 and 6 seat layouts come once a direction is picked.

t1.text: Start: from the Rule 0 table to the first turn

t2.text: Your own sheet: everything else, one marker away

t3.text: The end of the game, and the tablet

n1.text: The Rule 0 table page gains Start the game above Log this game. It is drawn simply here; the next round draws it over the real page. Seats, names and commander art come from the table.

n2.text: One screen, held by whoever started. Drag a face to where that player really sits. The layout follows the seat count (2 to 6). Starting life and who goes first can be changed here; nothing else to set.

n3.text: Each panel faces its player. The player whose turn it is gets End turn on their own panel: one tap passes it clockwise. The strip down the middle shows the round (it goes up once everyone has had a turn) and holds what the table shares and changes often: the monarch, the initiative, day/night, dice, and undo. A holder's face sits on its button.

n4.text: Players change their own life. Tap the + half to gain 1 and the − half to lose 1; hold to change by 10. The running change (−3) shows for 2 seconds, then saves as one entry. Undo in the strip takes back the last change. The screen edges ignore swipes.

n5.text: Counters: every player counter with a line of reminder text, plus city's blessing and dungeons. Only counters above 0 show on your panel as badges. Monarch, initiative and day/night moved to the strip.

n6.text: The marker on your panel opens your sheet, turned to face you, on Commander damage: the damage you TAKE, one card per opposing commander (two for a partner deck). It comes off your life too; 21 from one commander puts you out.

n7.text: Tax: count each cast from the command zone; the tax is worked out for you. A partner deck has one row per commander.

n8.text: Mana: floating mana by color, and storm. Clear empties it in one tap.

n9.text: Table: the shared things you need now and then, open from anyone's sheet so it faces whoever uses it. The game's history, and concede or end the game. Dice moved to the strip.

n10.text: A player at 0 life, 21 commander damage from one commander, or 10 poison is out: the panel turns face down with how and on what turn. Undo is right there for a mistake. Concede is in the Table tab.

n11.text: When one player is left, the result faces the phone's owner. Log this game opens the shipped log form filled in, and every seated player's log starts with their result. Rematch starts again at once with the same seats and life; this game stays ready to log from the Rule 0 table.

n12.text: A tablet lying flat: up to three players along each long side, panels facing them. Same panels, marker and sheets as the phone, with bigger numbers.

n13.text: Tap the crown in the strip and every panel becomes one big button: tap the new monarch's panel and it's done. The initiative works the same way. Day/night needs no picker: one tap makes it day, then each tap flips it.

p1.text: Try it. Tap the − and + halves; hold one to change by 10. Peter goes first: tap End turn on his panel and the turn moves clockwise; the round goes up after everyone has gone. Tap the crown or shield, then a panel, to pass it. Tap the sun to start day, again for night. Tap the dice button, pick d6, d20 or a coin, and it rolls across the table; tap it to roll again. Open a sheet with the marker and add commander damage to 21 to see a player go out. Undo takes back anything.

t4.text: From the quick-access research: badges, partners, rematch

q1.text: Badges on a panel are buttons. Tapping one never changes the value (a complaint about Lifelinker was that a tap meant to open counters changed life). It opens your sheet on that counter, highlighted, so the next tap is the +/−.

q2.text: A partner deck shows both commanders' art, split down the panel. Peter here plays Ishai + Bruse Tarl (the shipped partners fixture).

q3.text: Commander damage is one card per opponent. A partner deck's card splits its art and stacks one stepper per partner (21 from either one is lethal), so a partner never takes an extra column.

n12b.text: Four players: two per long side, each panel half the tablet. Same strip between the rows.

n12c.text: Five players: three on one side, two on the other. The pair's panels are wider, so whoever sits on the short side can take the seat on the side with room. Setup's seat map decides which side gets three.

q4.text: Stress test: six players and every deck has partners, so five opponent cards with two steppers each. Everything fits at 44px buttons with nothing cut off. Art and names here are stand-ins, only to test the space.

t5.text: Table layouts: where people sit, picked at setup

lay1.text: Setup gains a Table choice: tiny diagrams of the layouts that fit this many players, like the Companion's orientation picker. Picking one redraws the seat map, then faces drag into its seats. Options: 3 players, sides + end or all on one side; 4, two sides or one per side; 5, two sides or sides + end; 6, three per side or two per side + ends.

lay2.text: End seats sit on the phone's short edges. Their panels are wide and short, so the number sits beside the who row. The strip stays between the long sides. All on one side: every panel faces the same edge and the strip runs down the other.

lay3.text: Tablet with end seats: the end panels run the full height of each short edge. The two long sides keep the strip between them.

n2c.text: I'll pick: the line above the map changes to "Tap who goes first" and a tap rings that face with Goes first. Dragging still moves seats. Random: at Start, the die rolls across the table and lands on the first player's panel (it uses the 3D dice, loaded during setup).

ic1.text: Each icon's line says what it's based on. Orange = an official Magic symbol (poison, energy, tickets, day/night). Others follow the mechanic's helper card (rad, City's blessing, dungeon, initiative's Undercity, monarch, the Ring) or, with no official visual (experience, speed, storm, tax), what the mechanic does. The recommended picks for the Ring, speed and storm are in the set above; the alternatives are on the board below.

t7.text: Addendum · 7 or 8 seated: Start is off, and says why

s7.text: 7 or 8 seated: Start the game stays in its place, turned off, with the reason under it and the way out (Seats, top right). The table still seats 8, and Log this game and Close the table work as before.

t8.text: Addendum · A seat still picking its deck

s8.text: A seat still picking its deck doesn't block Start. The line under Start says what happens: tap it now and Max plays on a plain panel with his name ("no deck"), or wait for his art. Seats are snapshotted at Start, so a deck picked later doesn't join this game. Not the grey out art: at the table grey means out. The plain panel also replaces the tablet's off-theme guest blue.

t9.text: Addendum · Coming back to a saved game

s9.text: Reloading the tracker itself drops straight back into the game, with no prompt. Leave it and come back to the table page, and the game saved on this device sits at the top (desktop: top of the right column) in place of Start the game: who's in, their life, the round, whose turn. Back to the game picks it up. Discard this game drops it, with the shipped Undo toast. Only the device holding the game shows the card.

t10.text: Addendum · The table closes or reseats mid-game

s10.text: Seats are snapshotted at Start, so a reseat, a deck change or the table closing never interrupts play: the people still playing see nothing change. The closed table page keeps the game card, so the holder can get back to it. The result says when the table closed and how long it still logs (a host close keeps Log this game until 6 am), and Back to the table becomes Back to Friends. After a reseat, the log fills from the seats you played, not the table's new seats.

s11.text: Two ways to a draw. End game (Table tab) now asks how it ended: one big tile per player still in, plus A draw. Or the last players go out in the same change (their 2-second pending changes land together), and the game ends as a draw on its own. The finish screen splits the drawn players' art with an equals mark and lists who went out before. Log this game starts the log as Draw with no winner; players who went out earlier log a loss.
